subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should the remaining skill lifecycle work live in core Skill Workshop, in a plugin/API or ClawHub surface first, or be declined after the merged reactive-correction capture?
rationale: The remaining request changes how OpenClaw infers durable skill edits and when it hides or deletes user-authored skill artifacts, which is product policy plus persistent state/config design rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Design plugin/API boundary first
options.body: Define the metrics, proposal provenance, consent, and archive/restore contract outside a broad core implementation, extending core only where a plugin or ClawHub path cannot express the lifecycle safely.

options.title: Sponsor a core lifecycle design
options.body: Accept that skill repair and retirement are core Skill Workshop responsibilities, then require a narrowed design with opt-in config, SQLite-backed state, doctor/migration expectations, and focused proof before implementation.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Treat the merged reactive-correction capture as sufficient for now and decline automated retirement or performance-driven skill rewriting until stronger user demand appears.

recommendation.title: Design plugin/API boundary first
recommendation.body: Define the metrics, proposal provenance, consent, and archive/restore contract outside a broad core implementation, extending core only where a plugin or ClawHub path cannot express the lifecycle safely.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter shaped the merged capture invariant and is the clearest product-policy owner among the related history signals.
